missing: The actual dollar math: usable kWh per daily cycle × peak/off-peak spread minus round-trip losses, battery cycle-wear cost per kWh, and payback years for specific stations (and which models actually have a TOU/scheduled-bypass mode at what price).
why: One major reviewer (Popular Mechanics, appearing three times via Yahoo and AOL syndication) answers the exact question from hands-on experience with TOU-mode stations, but admits the savings are hard to estimate and gives no numbers. Everything else is utility or government TOU rate explainers that never mention power stations, a vague solar-installer blog, and three unreadable results. A page that does the arbitrage arithmetic for named stations with current prices would compete with Popular Mechanics but could win on specificity.
